questions.q: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria is noteworthy for establishing at the federal level
options: a diarchy under the military and political parties
an executive presidency with the President as both head of state and head of government
a parliamentary system headed by a Prime Minister
a rotating presidency among the six geopolitical zones
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution ended the Westminster-style parliamentary arrangement and introduced an executive President who combined the roles of head of state and head of government. A parliamentary system headed by a Prime Minister was associated with the independence era, while the other listed arrangements were not created by the 1979 Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an anomic pressure group?
options: A group that relies mainly on professional lobbying and legal representations to influence policy
A group that limits its activities to campaigns within the legislature
A group that expresses its demands through unlawful or violent actions such as riots and destruction of property
A group that is registered primarily to sponsor candidates in general elections
questions.explanation: Anomic pressure groups are largely spontaneous and often act outside normal political channels, sometimes through violent or disruptive protests. A group that lobbies professionally is more institutional, while one that sponsors candidates is acting like a political party.

questions.q: In Nigeria’s foreign policy, the principle of reciprocity means that Nigeria should
options: respond to the treatment given to its citizens and interests by another state in a similar manner
provide development aid to all countries that trade with Nigeria
give equal diplomatic recognition to every country in the world
join any international organisation that admits African states
questions.explanation: Reciprocity means that Nigeria responds to another state in a manner matching the treatment Nigeria or its citizens receive. It does not require automatic diplomatic recognition of every country, membership of every organisation admitting African states, or aid to every trading partner.

questions.q: Which form of government is characterised by the fusion of executive and legislative powers, with ministers being members of the legislature and accountable to it?
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive is drawn from the legislature and remains accountable to it, often through votes of confidence. A presidential system separates the executive from the legislature, while a confederal system concerns the distribution of power among component units and an oligarchy is rule by a small group.

questions.q: During military rule in Nigeria, laws made by state military administrators were known as...
questions.explanation: Federal military governments issued decrees, while state military administrators made edicts. An act is normally a law of a civilian legislature, and a bye-law is usually made by a local authority.

questions.q: In a democracy, the main value of a free press in relation to public opinion is that it...
options: replaces the legislature in making laws
guarantees that all citizens will share the same opinion
provides information and a platform for diverse views on public issues
determines the final decisions of the courts
questions.explanation: A free press helps form and express public opinion by informing the public and allowing debate. It does not make judicial or legislative decisions, nor does it make opinions uniform.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In Nigeria, where the President proclaims a state of emergency but the National Assembly may revoke the proclamation, this arrangement best illustrates
questions.explanation: The National Assembly's ability to revoke a presidential proclamation is a legislative check on executive action. Such mutual restraints among the arms are what checks and balances describe. Delegated legislation, collective responsibility and parliamentary supremacy deal with different constitutional ideas.

questions.q: At a ward election in Ilesa, the candidate with the highest number of valid votes is declared winner even though she did not obtain more than half of the total votes cast. This is a feature of
questions.explanation: In a plurality or first-past-the-post system, the candidate with the highest number of votes wins even without an absolute majority. The scenario describes that rule exactly. Proportional representation and party-list systems allocate seats according to party vote shares, while a run-off is used when no candidate reaches the required majority.

questions.q: The security of tenure granted to judges in Nigeria is principally intended to
options: make judges answerable only to the President
protect judges from undue interference in the performance of their duties
allow judges to amend the Constitution
ensure that judges remain in office even after committing grave misconduct
questions.explanation: Security of tenure protects judges by ensuring they can be removed only through a rigorous constitutional process, thereby reducing fear of political interference. It supports judicial independence so that judges can decide cases impartially. It does not make judges answerable only to the President, allow them to amend the Constitution, or protect them from removal for grave misconduct.

questions.q: In the administration of a ministry in Nigeria, the permanent secretary is mainly responsible for
options: day-to-day administration and implementation of government policy
questions.explanation: The permanent secretary is the chief administrative officer of a ministry who oversees day-to-day administration and implementation of policy. Law-making belongs to the legislature, election petitions to tribunals and courts, and command of the armed forces to the appropriate military authority.

questions.q: In a federal system like Nigeria, the power of a state government to legislate on matters in the concurrent legislative list is subject to the condition that the state law does not conflict with an existing federal law. This arrangement illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Concurrent powers are shared by the federal and state legislatures; where a state law conflicts with a valid federal law on the same concurrent matter, the federal law prevails. Exclusive powers belong only to the federal government, while residual matters fall mainly to the states without a concurrent federal law.

questions.q: Under the 1960 Independence Constitution, the Governor-General represented the Queen while the Prime Minister was the
questions.explanation: The 1960 Constitution retained the Queen as ceremonial Head of State, represented by the Governor-General, while the Prime Minister led the government. The office of President as Head of State came with the 1963 Republican Constitution.

questions.q: After a party wins a governorship election in Kaduna State, it appoints many loyal party members as commissioners and board members. This practice is best described as
questions.explanation: Patronage is the use of appointments or benefits to reward party loyalists and supporters after electoral victory. Lobbying is an attempt to influence legislators or officials, while a coalition is an alliance of parties or groups.

questions.q: A form of government in which political power is held by a small group of people regarded as the most qualified to rule is called
questions.explanation: Aristocracy is rule by a small group regarded as the best qualified. Autocracy is rule by one person, plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, and theocracy is rule based on religious authority.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates the principle of separation of powers under a presidential system?
options: The president dissolves the legislature whenever a bill is rejected.
The cabinet is drawn from and answers to the legislature.
The judiciary is under the direct control of the president.
The legislature, executive and judiciary are vested in separate organs and exercise their powers independently.
questions.explanation: Separation of powers means that law-making, implementation and interpretation are assigned to distinct organs that exercise their functions independently. A cabinet answering directly to the legislature is more typical of a parliamentary system, while presidential control over the judiciary would violate the principle.

questions.q: The military Head of State who handed over power to Alhaji Shehu Shagari in 1979 was
questions.explanation: Olusegun Obasanjo's military administration supervised the transition programme and handed over to Shehu Shagari on 1 October 1979. Gowon was overthrown in 1975, Murtala died in 1976, and Buhari came to power in 1983.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of military rule in Nigeria?
options: Laws were made mainly through decrees rather than by elected legislatures.
The judiciary had final authority to declare decrees unconstitutional.
Political parties competed freely without restriction.
Elections were held regularly to determine the tenure of the Head of State.
questions.explanation: Military governments in Nigeria suspended or modified the constitution and ruled largely by decree. Many decrees contained ouster clauses that restricted court review, and political party activity was usually restricted.

questions.q: A person who has full membership of a state and enjoys political rights such as voting and holding public office is known as
questions.explanation: A citizen has full membership of a state, including political rights and obligations such as obedience to the law. A resident may live in a place without full political rights, an alien owes allegiance to another state, and a refugee has a special protection status.

questions.q: The United Nations agency responsible for protecting and assisting refugees and displaced persons is the
options: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
questions.explanation: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees is the UN agency mandated to protect refugees and assist displaced persons. The United Nations Development Programme focuses on development, the World Health Organization on health, and the United Nations Children's Fund on children.

questions.q: Constitutionalism is best described as the principle that government should
options: have unlimited power to maintain order
be controlled only by the armed forces
be limited by law and operate according to constitutional rules
derive its authority solely from tradition
questions.explanation: Constitutionalism means limited government, in which rulers are bound by law and constitutional procedures. Unlimited power, military control or reliance on tradition alone contradicts the idea of constitutional government.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In Kano State, the governor presents a proposed budget of ₦45 billion to the State House of Assembly for debate and approval before funds are spent. This practice best demonstrates
options: delegation of legislative powers to the governor
questions.explanation: The power of the House of Assembly to debate and approve the budget is a check by the legislature on the executive's control of public funds. It is not the governor controlling the legislature, nor is it delegation of legislative powers to him.

questions.q: Professor Bello, a Vice-Chancellor in Jos, issues directives that staff obey because university statutes and conditions of service confer on his office the power to do so. The type of authority he is exercising is
questions.explanation: Obedience is based on formal rules and the legal office held by the Vice-Chancellor, which is legal-rational authority. Traditional authority rests on custom, charismatic authority rests on personal qualities, and coercive authority relies on force.

questions.q: In a local government election in Ilorin East, Amina scored 2,100 votes, her closest rival scored 1,900 votes, and other candidates shared 900 votes. Amina was declared elected although she did not obtain more than half of the valid votes. This electoral system is
questions.explanation: The total valid votes were 4,900, so more than half is 2,450; Amina had 2,100 but was still elected because she had the highest number of votes. This is the first-past-the-post or plurality system. A second-ballot system would require a run-off when no candidate obtained an absolute majority.

questions.q: Voter registration is important in an election mainly because it
options: determines the amount of tax payable by each candidate
enables political parties to appoint polling officers
decides the number of seats won by each party in advance
identifies persons qualified to vote and helps prevent multiple voting
questions.explanation: The voters' register identifies those entitled to vote and helps guard against multiple or fraudulent voting. It does not fix candidates' taxes, appoint polling officers, or determine party seats before voting takes place.

questions.q: At a constituency level in a Nigerian general election, the official responsible for collating the results from polling units and declaring the winner is the
questions.explanation: The returning officer collates the constituency results and declares the winner. A presiding officer manages activities at a polling unit, while party agents and electoral observers witness the process but do not declare results.

questions.q: The Auditor-General for the Federation is constitutionally required to submit reports on public accounts to the
options: Secretary to the Government of the Federation
questions.explanation: The Auditor-General for the Federation audits public accounts and submits the report to the National Assembly, which considers it through its Public Accounts Committees. The Chief Justice, Secretary to the Government of the Federation and Federal Executive Council do not receive such audit reports as their primary constitutional responsibility.

questions.q: Local governments in Nigeria are often described as a third tier of government mainly because they
options: appoint judges of state High Courts
are constitutionally recognised with assigned functions and revenue from the Federation Account
conduct elections into the State House of Assembly
questions.explanation: Local governments are described as a third tier because the Constitution recognises them, assigns functions to them and makes financial provisions for them from the Federation Account. They do not conduct state assembly elections, appoint High Court judges or control the armed forces.

questions.q: The Nigerian Medical Association advises its members to withdraw emergency cover in public hospitals until the Federal Government increases health workers' allowances. This action best illustrates
options: a political party trying to win public office
the exercise of judicial review by a professional body
the Federal Government carrying out delegated legislation
the use of industrial action by a pressure group to influence government policy
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Medical Association is acting as a pressure group by using industrial action to press the government for better allowances. The action is not a political party seeking office, nor is it judicial review or delegated legislation.

questions.q: Nigeria’s role in the 2017 ECOWAS mediation that persuaded President Yahya Jammeh to concede defeat in The Gambia is best described as an example of
options: pursuit of permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council
support for constitutional order and peaceful transfer of power in West Africa
protection of Nigerian commercial interests in The Gambia
implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area
questions.explanation: The mediation sought to prevent an unconstitutional extension of tenure and uphold The Gambia’s election result. It is therefore linked to Nigeria’s commitment to constitutional government and stability within ECOWAS, not to Security Council ambitions, narrow commercial protection or trade-area implementation.

questions.q: Which body was established to conduct research and training in international affairs and advise the Nigerian government on foreign policy?
options: Nigerian Institute of Advanced Legal Studies
National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies
National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Institute of International Affairs is the foreign-affairs think tank that undertakes research and training and offers policy advice. The National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies has a broader policy mandate, while the legal and legislative institutes specialise in law and legislative studies.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major limitation on the formation of sound public opinion in Nigeria?
options: Widespread illiteracy and limited access to reliable information
The existence of a free and plural press
The activities of civil society organisations
The regular conduct of elections by the electoral commission
questions.explanation: Sound public opinion depends on access to accurate information and the ability to assess issues critically; illiteracy and poor access to reliable information hinder this. A free press, regular elections and civil society groups generally help rather than limit the formation of informed public opinion.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: In a presidential system, the legislature can remove the President only through impeachment, while the President cannot dissolve the legislature. This arrangement best illustrates
options: separation of powers with checks and balances
fusion of executive and legislative functions
questions.explanation: The President and the legislature have separate tenures and powers, but the legislature still has a check through impeachment. This is the essence of separation of powers combined with checks and balances, not a fusion of the two arms as in a parliamentary system.

questions.q: A government that secures obedience mainly by deploying soldiers, police and threats of detention is relying on
questions.explanation: Coercive power is exercised through force, threats or punishment, such as the use of soldiers and threats of detention. Traditional authority and charismatic authority rest on custom and personal appeal respectively, while legitimate authority depends on acceptance of the right to rule.

questions.q: In a constituency election, Amina polled 22,000 votes, Bala 14,000, Chidi 9,000 and Dauda 3,000. Which statement correctly describes the result under the first-past-the-post system?
options: Bala wins because the candidate with the second-highest votes is declared winner when no candidate has an absolute majority.
Amina wins because she obtained the highest number of valid votes.
No candidate wins because Amina did not obtain an absolute majority of the valid votes.
Amina wins because she obtained more than half of the total valid votes.
questions.explanation: Under first-past-the-post, the candidate with the highest number of valid votes wins, so Amina wins with 22,000 votes. She did not obtain an absolute majority, which would require more than 24,000 votes, but that is not a condition for victory in this system.

questions.q: In a country using a party-list proportional representation system with no electoral threshold, 200 parliamentary seats are to be shared according to votes as follows: Alliance for Progress 40%, People's Trust 30%, Unity Forum 20% and Green Agenda 10%. How many seats should Unity Forum receive?
questions.explanation: Under a party-list proportional representation system without a threshold, seats are allocated in proportion to votes won. Unity Forum's 20% share of 200 seats is (20 ÷ 100) × 200 = 40 seats.

questions.q: The Supreme Court strikes down a section of an Act of the National Assembly for being inconsistent with the Constitution. This power is known as
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine laws and executive actions and declare them unconstitutional when inconsistent with the Constitution. Judicial precedent concerns following earlier court decisions, while certiorari is an order quashing a lower tribunal's decision.

questions.q: A state House of Assembly in Nigeria makes a law on a matter that is neither in the Exclusive Legislative List nor the Concurrent Legislative List. Such a matter is classified as a
questions.explanation: Residual matters are those not placed in the Exclusive Legislative List or the Concurrent Legislative List, and state governments generally legislate on them. Exclusive matters are for the National Assembly alone, while concurrent matters fall within both federal and state legislative competence.

questions.q: A major change introduced by the Republican Constitution of 1963 was that
options: Nigeria adopted a presidential system of government.
the Queen ceased to be Nigeria's Head of State.
the office of the Prime Minister was abolished.
appeals from Nigerian courts to the Privy Council were made compulsory.
questions.explanation: The 1963 Republican Constitution replaced the Queen with a President as Nigeria's Head of State, while the Prime Minister remained head of government. The presidential system came with the 1979 Constitution, and appeals to the Privy Council were abolished rather than made compulsory.

questions.q: During a general election, two political parties agree to support a single candidate in order to defeat the ruling party. This arrangement is best described as...
questions.explanation: An arrangement between parties to support a common candidate before or during an election is an electoral alliance. A coalition government is formed after an election when parties share ministerial power, while a bye-election and a pressure-group merger are different processes.

questions.q: When Nigeria supports ECOWAS sanctions against a member state where the military has overthrown a civilian government, Nigeria is principally demonstrating its commitment to...
options: the promotion of free trade only
questions.explanation: Nigeria’s action is aimed at upholding constitutional government and restoring stability within the ECOWAS sub-region. Non-alignment does not mean indifference to unconstitutional rule, and the measure is political rather than purely commercial.

questions.q: The significance of Nigeria serving as a non-permanent member of the United Nations Security Council is that Nigeria...
options: participates for a limited term in decisions on international peace and security
ceases to be a member of ECOWAS for the period of service
automatically becomes the Secretary-General of the United Nations
obtains a permanent veto over all decisions of the Security Council
questions.explanation: A non-permanent member is elected for a temporary term and takes part in the Security Council’s work on peace and security, but it does not have the permanent veto of the five permanent members. The office of Secretary-General is separate, and UN service does not affect ECOWAS membership.

questions.q: At the end of the Nigerian Civil War in 1970, the military government of General Yakubu Gowon declared 'No victor, no vanquished'. The main aim of the declaration was to...
options: promote reconciliation and reintegration of the former secessionist areas
divide the country into two separate military zones
punish all former Biafran soldiers and officials
hand over power to a civilian government immediately
questions.explanation: The declaration was part of the post-war reconciliation, rehabilitation and reconstruction policy designed to heal divisions and reintegrate the affected areas. It was not intended to punish the defeated side, partition Nigeria or effect an immediate transfer of power.

questions.q: A foreigner who has resided in Nigeria for the period prescribed by law and satisfies the President that he is of good character may become a Nigerian citizen through
questions.explanation: Naturalisation is the process by which an adult foreigner who meets residence, character and other statutory conditions acquires Nigerian citizenship. Citizenship by registration is used mainly for certain persons linked to Nigeria by marriage or descent, while citizenship by descent depends on parentage.

questions.q: Nigeria became a member of the United Nations in
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the United Nations in 1960 after attaining independence. The country’s admission to the world body marked the beginning of its active participation in UN affairs.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: The provision that a judge can be removed from office only on stated grounds and through a special procedure is intended to promote
questions.explanation: Security of tenure and a special removal procedure protect judges from arbitrary political pressure. Such protection supports independent adjudication rather than control of the courts by the executive or legislature.

questions.q: Which of the following best enhances the legitimacy of a government?
options: control of state-owned media to praise the government
frequent use of force against political opponents
appointment of relatives to key public offices
observance of constitutional procedures in assuming and exercising power
questions.explanation: Legitimacy is the acceptance of a government as rightful, and it is strengthened when power is acquired and used according to constitutional rules. Force, media propaganda and nepotism may produce obedience, but they do not make a government widely accepted as legitimate.

questions.q: Following the death of a senator in Kogi State, a by-election is conducted mainly to
options: choose local government chairmen after their councils are dissolved
fill a vacancy in a legislative seat that occurs between general elections
elect members of the State Executive Council
determine the candidate of a political party for a general election
questions.explanation: A by-election fills a vacant legislative seat between general elections. It is not used to select party candidates or to constitute the state executive or local government councils.

questions.q: Question time in a legislature is mainly used to
options: elect the presiding officers of the legislature
conduct the second reading of a bill
demand explanations from ministers about the conduct of public affairs
questions.explanation: Question time enables members to ask ministers for explanations and accounts of public affairs. It is not the stage for second reading, choosing presiding officers, or settling inter-state disputes.

questions.q: The type of political party that seeks to attract members from all sections of society and appeals to a broad range of interests is known as a
questions.explanation: A mass party tries to enrol a large membership and appeal to many social groups, unlike a cadre or elite party with restricted membership. A splinter party is a breakaway group and is not defined by broad membership.

questions.q: The Nigerian Technical Aid Corps, through which Nigerian professionals serve in other developing countries, was established in 1987 during the administration of
questions.explanation: The Technical Aid Corps was established in 1987 under General Ibrahim Babangida to send Nigerian professionals to assist other developing countries. It was not established under the Murtala Mohammed, Shagari or Abacha administrations.

questions.q: The current headquarters of the Economic Community of West African States is located in
questions.explanation: The current headquarters of ECOWAS is in Abuja, Nigeria. The organisation was established in Lagos in 1975, but Lagos is not its present headquarters.

questions.q: Under a unitary system of government,
options: the central government is subordinate to the component units
powers are shared between the central government and component units by a written constitution
component units have the right to secede from the central government
a single central government exercises supreme authority over the whole country
questions.explanation: In a unitary system, one central government holds supreme authority, although it may create local units for administration. Any devolved powers are granted by the centre and can be withdrawn, unlike a federation where powers are constitutionally shared.

questions.q: The 1976 local government reform under the military administration of General Olusegun Obasanjo is notable mainly for
options: recognising local governments as the third tier of government
giving local governments the power to establish their own police forces
transferring the Nigeria Police Force to local councils
creating the office of elected state governors
questions.explanation: The 1976 reform introduced a uniform local government system and recognised local governments as the third tier of government. It did not transfer the Nigeria Police Force to local councils, and local governments do not establish separate police forces.

questions.q: The ECOWAS Standby Force was established mainly to
options: issue a single West African passport
supervise elections in all member states
respond to security crises and support peace operations in West Africa
collect customs duties at ECOWAS borders
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Standby Force is a security arrangement meant to respond to crises and support peace operations in West Africa. Customs duties, election supervision and passports are handled through other ECOWAS institutions and protocols.

questions.q: A proposed alteration to an entrenched section of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria requires, among other things, the support of
options: a simple majority in the National Assembly and approval by all state governors
a simple majority in the State Houses of Assembly alone
a unanimous vote in both chambers of the National Assembly
at least two-thirds of all members of each House of the National Assembly and approval by the Houses of Assembly of at least two-thirds of the states
questions.explanation: Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution requires a special majority of at least two-thirds of all members of each House of the National Assembly, as well as approval by the Houses of Assembly of at least two-thirds of the states, before the proposed alteration is presented for assent. A simple majority or the votes of governors alone cannot alter an entrenched provision.

questions.topic: Separation of powers and checks and balances
questions.q: A state governor also serves as the Speaker of the State House of Assembly and presides over legislative sittings. The principle most clearly violated is
questions.explanation: Separation of powers requires the executive, legislature and judiciary to be kept in distinct hands so that one person or body does not control more than one arm. A governor presiding over legislative sittings combines executive and legislative roles. Collective responsibility and federalism concern different arrangements of government.

questions.q: Traders in Onitsha close their shops after a task force warning, not because they accept the directive as lawful but to avoid arrest. The governor’s ability to secure compliance is best described as
questions.explanation: Compliance here rests on fear of force or punishment, which is an example of coercive power. Authority would involve acceptance of the ruler’s right to give the directive. Traditional, legal-rational and charismatic authority are forms of accepted authority, not mere coercion.

questions.q: By ratifying an international agreement that imposes common tariffs, a state may be said to
options: exercise its sovereignty by accepting binding obligations
surrender its constitution to an international body
questions.explanation: A sovereign state can voluntarily accept treaty obligations and thereby limit how it exercises some powers without losing sovereignty entirely. Ratifying a tariff agreement does not transfer the people’s legitimacy to foreign states. It also does not place the state’s constitution under an international body.

questions.q: A country using a party-list proportional representation system has 120 legislative seats and no electoral threshold. If a party receives 35% of the valid votes, it should be allocated approximately
questions.explanation: Under proportional representation, seats are shared in proportion to votes. Here, 35% of 120 seats is 0.35 × 120 = 42 seats. A party with 35% of the votes does not automatically receive all the seats or only the same number as its percentage.

questions.q: In a presidential system of government, the executive is usually separated from the legislature because the president
options: is appointed by the supreme court to enforce the constitution
is chosen by parliament from among its members and remains in office while he commands majority support
is nominated by political parties and confirmed by the judiciary for life
is elected independently and serves a fixed term unless removed by impeachment
questions.explanation: A presidential executive is elected separately from the legislature and serves a fixed term, so it does not depend on a parliamentary vote of confidence to remain in office. The arrangement in which the executive is chosen by parliament and stays while it commands majority support belongs to the parliamentary system.
